resources.string: Tip: scanning all categories fetches price history from ESI per profitable item — enable EVE Ref bulk data in Settings to make history lookups local and instant.
Finds items with profitable spread between buy and sell orders at the same station
Finds items priced low in the buy region that sell for more in the sell region
Select a category from the sidebar or search for an item.
Downloading EVE Static Data Export…\nThis may take a minute.
History will be loaded when you select a type.
No market history yet for this item.
* moving-average cost (resets when the position closes), before fees; the Orders tab has exact FIFO. Fees: %1$s (tax + broker).

How many days of price history define "normal" for this item -- Avg/High/Low/Volatility and the vs Avg discount are all computed over this window. It's not a wait time: ESI already has up to ~13 months of history, so results appear immediately. It's also the window the Backtest column re-checks on every single simulated day across all available history, not just once.
Skip items whose median daily trade volume (over the lookback window) is below this -- too thin to reliably trade.
Only include items currently at least this % below their own Lookback-day average price -- the core "is it cheap" filter. Items you hold or have orders on are always shown, whatever the filters.
Skip items whose price swings less than this % (std-dev ÷ average) over the lookback window -- too flat to dip deep enough, or rebound far enough, to beat a round trip's fees. 0 = no limit.
Skip items whose price swings more than this % (std-dev ÷ average) over the lookback window. 0 = no limit.

Skip items whose current price is at or below their own lowest recorded price in roughly the last year. A break to a new multi-month low looks like structural decline (e.g. made obsolete by a balance patch), not a routine dip worth feeding the buy ladder.
Filters out items whose recent price/volume history shows a sharp one-off spike (e.g. a buyout or wash trading).
A day's price counts as a spike if it's at least this many times the surrounding baseline.
A day's trade volume counts as a spike if it's at least this many times the surrounding baseline.

Total ISK you want invested across these items, including what you already hold -- a target exposure, not new money. Split across the picked candidates below, weighted by discount depth × daily traded ISK value; each item's To Buy is its share minus what you already hold.

How many of the top-ranked candidates get a share of the budget -- ranked by real ISK opportunity (discount % × daily traded value), not by raw discount % alone, so a deep discount on a thin/illiquid item doesn't crowd out a shallower discount on a liquid, high-value one.
Caps any single item at this % of the total budget, regardless of how deep its discount is.
Second cap: never allocate more than this many days' worth of the item's own median daily trading value -- avoids parking more ISK in one material than the market could plausibly absorb.
How many price rungs to split each item's allocation into. Anchored to your real average cost when you're already holding and underwater, otherwise to the current live price.

Price gap between each ladder rung. Later rungs (further price drops) get a bigger share of the item's allocation -- buy more the further it falls. Also the take-profit %: the sell target is your cost (incl. buy broker fee) + this %, net of sales tax and broker fee -- and the Backtest sells at the same rule.

Check rows below, then press %1$s to step through every checked item's buy-ladder rungs: opens the item's market window and copies the target price, then on the next press copies the quantity -- paste each into EVE's buy-order dialog.
Whether the second hotkey press (per rung) also copies the suggested quantity, or just advances.

Create alerts for every checked row at once (all rows if none are checked): buy-ladder rungs plus sell targets for held positions. Existing identical alerts are skipped. AlertMonitor fetches each item's order book once, however many alerts it has.
Pick a category (defaults to Manufacture & Research > Materials) and click Analyze
Select all / none -- checked rows feed the hotkey queue.
Live top buy order price -- the current best bid. This tab is built around placing your own buy orders, not instant-buying, so ladder prices are targets for standing orders, not asks to pay.
Average price over the Lookback-day window.

Your current holding: real quantity from your assets (all locations) plus stock listed in your sell orders, @ the moving-average cost of your tracked market buys, reset each time the position was fully sold (before broker fee; not FIFO, and stock from mining/reprocessing/manufacturing has no buy price to count). Anchors the buy ladder to your real entry instead of the live price.
How far below the Lookback-window's highest price the current price sits.
How far below the Lookback-window average the current price sits -- the core "is it cheap" number this tab ranks candidates by.
Price change over the last 7 days.

Replays this tab's strategy over up to a year of this item's own daily history: buy on every day the price is Min Discount % under the trailing Lookback-day average, and sell the whole position once selling nets cost + Ladder Step % (the same take-profit as the sell target), then wait for the next dip. Broker fee on buys, sales tax + broker fee on sells. Format: total P&L% (worst P&L% along the way), both vs the most capital tied up at once. A negative first number means the pattern hasn't historically paid off for this item. Uses the Ladder Step % from the last Analyze.
Price swinginess over the lookback window (std-dev ÷ average). Higher = choppier.
Median daily trade volume over the lookback window.
Held positions only: net profit selling the whole stack at the current lowest ask, after sales tax and broker fee, against your average cost including the broker fee you paid to buy.
That profit as % of what the held stack cost you.

ISK left to buy: this item's share of the budget (after ranking, the per-item cap and the liquidity cap) minus what you already hold at cost (incl. buy broker fee) and ISK in your open buy orders. Ladder quantities leave room for the broker fee. 0 once the position is full.
Buy: still below its share of the budget -- place the buy ladder below.
Wait: position is full, sell target not reached yet.
Sell: selling at the lowest ask already nets your cost (incl. buy broker fee) + take-profit, after sales tax and broker fee.
Buying: your buy orders already cover the rest of this item's allocation.
On sale: your stock is listed in sell orders -- waiting for fills.

Recent price or volume spike detected -- a sharp one-off jump (e.g. a single large buyout, or wash trading) rather than an organic move. Doesn't exclude the item by itself (Spike Filter is set to "Any"); check the price chart (chart icon next to the name) before trusting the ladder on this one.

Create price alerts (Alerts tab) for this item: remaining buy-ladder rungs (top buy order falls to the rung) and, for a held position, the sell target (lowest ask rises to it). Skips levels already crossed and alerts that already exist.
Create alerts for this item's buy ladder

Target price for a standing buy order → ISK to spend at that rung, broker fee included (the rung's quantity leaves room for it). * = already at/above the current top bid, so it's actionable right now rather than a future target.
Your active market orders on this item (from the last Orders sync).

Sell the whole stack in one order at or above the target: your cost (incl. buy broker fee) + take-profit %, net of sales tax and broker fee. "now" is the net profit selling everything at the current lowest ask, after the same fees.
Current best buy order at the station — the price your own buy order has to beat.
Current best sell order at the station — the price your own sell order has to undercut.
Net profit per unit after sales tax and broker fees, as % of the sell price.
Net profit per unit as % of the buy price — return on the ISK you tie up.
Profit per unit after sales tax and broker fees on both orders.
Price change over the last 7 days.
Units traded per day in the region (from market history), capped by real station fills when Adam4EVE Flow is on and scaled by Vol % when enabled.
Rough daily profit: net per unit × daily volume. Assumes you get your share of the flow — real results depend on competition.
Price you pay in the buy region — the lowest sell order or your own buy order, depending on the trade type.
Price you get in the sell region — the highest buy order or your own sell order, depending on the trade type.
Net profit per unit after fees and shipping, as % of the sell price.
Net profit per unit as % of what you spend (buy price + shipping).
Cargo volume of one unit (packaged for ships).
Hauling cost per unit — from ISK/m³, or Ship % of Cost when that is enabled.
Profit per unit after taxes, broker fees and shipping.
Price change over the last 7 days.
Units traded per day — in the sell region, or the buy region when Src vol % is selected.
Suggested quantity: what the order books can actually supply at a profit, capped by daily volume (and Adam4EVE flow when on).
Total expected profit for the suggested quantity.
Number of competing sell / buy orders at the station. Many orders = more fighting over the same flow.
Your selected character's sales tax and broker fee (set in Settings → Character Fees). Used in every profit calculation.
Hide items whose net margin (after fees) is below this %.
Hide items that trade fewer units per day than this — too slow to turn over.
Hide items whose buy price is above this (ISK) — limits how much capital one unit ties up.
Hide items whose net profit per unit (ISK) is below this.
When checked, scales the daily volume by this % — e.g. 20 if you expect to get about a fifth of the market. Affects Est. Daily and the copied quantity.
Hide items you already have active orders for.
Cap volume by real per-station buy/sell fills from Adam4EVE instead of trusting region-wide history. Uses a third-party service.
A day counts as a price spike if its price is at least this many times the surrounding baseline.
A day counts as a volume spike if its traded volume is at least this many times the surrounding baseline.
How many recent days of history are checked for spikes.
Whether the hotkey's second press copies the suggested quantity, or just moves to the next item.
When checked, the assumed sell price is capped at buy price + this %, so a thin or unreliable destination market can't inflate the profit.
Hauling cost per m³ of cargo, used to price shipping.
When checked, shipping is priced as this % of the cargo's value instead of by volume — closer to courier contracts for expensive, small items.
Skip items where a single unit is bigger than this (m³) — too bulky to haul.
The % of daily volume you expect to trade. Checked: based on the buy (source) region's volume; unchecked: on the sell (destination) region's.
Cap the legs that are your own placed orders by real per-station fills from Adam4EVE. Uses a third-party service.
Saved buy/sell region + station routes — load one to switch quickly.
Gap between the best sell and best buy price, as % of the buy price. A wide spread leaves room for station trading.
Units still left in the order / units it was originally placed with.
Price × remaining units — total ISK sitting in the order.
Minimum quantity per transaction the order owner requires.
How far from its station a buy order accepts sellers: station, a number of jumps, or the whole region.
When the order was placed or its price last changed.
Time left until the order expires.

How each leg is traded. "Sell" = take the lowest sell order (instant buy); "Buy" = hit the highest buy order (instant sell); "order" = place your own order and wait. Safe Buy → Sell prices your buy order below what local traders could profit from, so it's rarely outbid.
Items whose recent history shows a sharp one-off spike (a buyout, wash trading) can look profitable when they aren't. Exclude them, show only them, or ignore.
The alert fires once the watched price goes below (or above) this value. Checked every 5 minutes while the app is running.
Saved region + station pairs — pick one to switch without searching.
